## Potential Duplicate PRs Found

I found two related PRs that appear to address similar permission inheritance issues:

1. **PR #29235** - `fix(task): respect subagent explicit edit:allow over inherited parent edit:deny`
   - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/29235
   - Directly addresses subagent permission inheritance with explicit allow overriding parent deny rules

2. **PR #27654** - `fix(task): subagent explicit edit:allow overrides parent edit:deny`
   - https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/27654
   - Similar focus on subagent edit permissions and deny rule handling

Both PRs appear to be addressing the same core issue as the current PR #29778: how subagent permissions should inherit from parent rules, specifically regarding edit/deny rule precedence. These should be reviewed to ensure they're not overlapping work or if they're related iterations of the same fix.

> When the 'orchestrator' style agent with no permissions delegates the subagent, the edit: allow is ignored.

This is to prevent permission leakage, e.g., the Plan agent delegating to another agent to write on its behalf.

I added the PR above to find a middle ground, where if you have a matching `edit` permission rule between the parent agent and subagent, the rule won't be added to the new session's permission ruleset. This means that global `deny` permissions won't be added to the end of the list and overrule your other edit permissions (permissions match in a [LIFO order](https://opencode.ai/docs/permissions/#granular-rules-object-syntax).
This PR also addresses the "regression" mentioned in [PR 27201](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/pull/27201#issuecomment-4468739441)

Follow-up from further testing: the behavior is slightly different than described in the original report.

With `"bash": "allow"` set in `opencode.json`, the command executes and the agent receives the output — but Zed's ACP panel shows "Awaiting Confirmation" for the same tool call, with no way to resolve it.

So the actual sequence is:
1. Zed surfaces an approval prompt in the ACP panel
2. The command executes and returns output to the agent *before* the user can respond
3. Zed is left with an unresolvable "Awaiting Confirmation" prompt

This is closer to the race condition described in #29422 than a silent drop. The prompt appears, but it is already stale by the time the user sees it. Approval or denial has no effect on the outcome.

> ## Root cause: `auth.json` corrupted with whitespace-only contents
> I hit this on Windows 11 with opencode 1.15.5 and traced it to a specific failure mode that I think explains every "Ctrl+C while building" / "closed the terminal mid-build" report above. Posting the diagnosis in case it helps the maintainers and the next person who lands here.
> 
> ### What the server is actually crashing on
> The TUI-facing error (`4 of 5 requests failed: config.providers, provider.list, app.agents, config.get`) is downstream noise. The real failure in the server log is a JSON parse error inside `Auth.all()`:
> 
> ```
> ERROR ... service=server error=JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token ' '
>     cause=SyntaxError: JSON Parse error: Unrecognized token ' '
>     at FileSystem.readJson (chunk-y6vv15b7.js)
>     at Auth.all (chunk-y6vv15b7.js)
>     at Config.loadInstanceState (chunk-y6vv15b7.js)
>     at Config.state (chunk-y6vv15b7.js)
>     at Config.get (chunk-hqfz04v1.js)
> ```
> 
> Every config-dependent request goes through `Config.get` -> `Config.loadInstanceState` -> `Auth.all` -> `readJson(auth.json)`. When that parse throws, every one of those requests fails with the same generic "Unexpected server error", which is why the user sees four failures instead of one. Logs live at `~/.local/share/opencode/log/*.log` (or `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\log\` on Windows) — searching them for `Auth.all` surfaces the cause immediately.
> 
> ### What the files looked like
> On my machine, **both** `auth.json` files existed and were non-empty, but contained only whitespace — no JSON, not a single `{`:
> 
> Path	Size	Contents
> `%LOCALAPPDATA%\opencode\auth.json`	327 bytes	327 space characters
> `%USERPROFILE%\.local\share\opencode\auth.json`	543 bytes	543 space characters
> Both files had identical modification timestamps down to the second.
> 
> ### Why this happens
> The byte counts strongly suggest a **non-atomic write**. The file is opened with `O_TRUNC`, the buffer is padded with spaces, and the actual JSON payload is supposed to overwrite that padding before the file is closed — but if the process is killed (Ctrl+C, terminal closed, OS shutdown) before the write completes, the file is left at its full size, filled with `0x20`. The filesystem still sees a "valid" non-empty file, so nothing flags it as broken.
> 
> This matches every report above where the problem started after interrupting opencode while it was "Building". That's the window in which the auth file is being rewritten.
> 
> The parser then fails fatally instead of treating an unreadable auth file as "no credentials configured", which traps the user: they cannot open the TUI to run `auth login`, because the TUI refuses to bootstrap without a parseable auth file. Catch-22.
> 
> ### Recovery (no reinstall needed)
> Overwrite both files with an empty JSON object, then re-authenticate. This worked instantly on my machine and preserves sessions, config, plugins, etc.
> 
> **Windows (PowerShell):**
> 
> Set-Content "$env:LOCALAPPDATA\opencode\auth.json" '{}'
> Set-Content "$env:USERPROFILE\.local\share\opencode\auth.json" '{}'
> opencode auth login
> **macOS / Linux:**
> 
> echo '{}' > "$HOME/.local/share/opencode/auth.json"
> # also check $XDG_DATA_HOME/opencode/auth.json if you've overridden it
> opencode auth login
> The "uninstall + nuke `.cache`, `.config`, `.local/share`" workaround posted earlier works because it deletes the corrupted file along with everything else. The targeted fix is just the two `auth.json` files — no need to lose your sessions, projects, or installed plugins.
> 
> ### Suggested fixes
> 1. **Atomic write for `auth.json`** — write to `auth.json.tmp` and `rename()` over `auth.json`. POSIX `rename` and Windows `MoveFileEx` with `MOVEFILE_REPLACE_EXISTING` are both atomic at the filesystem level: an interrupted process either leaves the old file intact or replaces it with the fully-written new one, never a half-written state. This eliminates the failure

I did have a little bit of trouble with the rebase (mainly a type issue):

```
ERROR 2026-05-28T19:17:04 +7ms service=session.processor session.id=ses_18ffb38dfffevEkEUR3HoEoRAS messageID=msg_e7004c75a001ZBSe0JUaTxgXqX error=tools.8.custom.input_schema.type: Field required stack=AI_APICallError: tools.8.custom.input_schema.type: Field required
```

According to my local agent:

```
Root Cause                                                                                          
                                                                                                    
The error tools.8.custom.input_schema.type: Field required is caused by the terminal tool's Schema. 
Union(...) parameter definition producing a JSON schema with "anyOf" at the top level but no "type":
"object". Anthropic's API requires "type": "object" at the root of every tool's input_schema.       

 The terminal tool is the only builtin tool using Schema.Union. Every other builtin uses Schema.Struct(
 ...), which always produces {"type": "object", ...}.                                                  
                                                                                                       
 The json-schema.ts normalization handles some anyOf simplifications (single-element, null-stripping,  
 empty-struct), but none apply to a 5-variant union. The ProviderTransform.schema() has no Anthropic-  
 specific handling for this case.                                                                      

```

@joshue031 will there be an Opencode API exposed, so that if not using the macOS app we can call it on demand? In my use case, I'd like to compact any idle session that has never been compacted after `n` seconds.

This in turn, dovetails nicely with conservative [Hindsight plugin settings](https://hindsight.vectorize.io/guides/2026/04/16/guide-opencode-memory-with-hindsight) and allows short sessions, that don't reach a high number of turns, to be guaranteed retention in Hindsight via an "_at least once_" compaction.

Hindsight Opencode plugin settings:
```json
"autoRetain": true,
"retainMode": "full-session",
"retainEveryNTurns": 100,
```

With these settings you get extremely conservative LLM usage happening every 100 turns. Sessions under 100 turns that don't get compacted wouldn't get retained into memory. If an API was exposed, a process could audit Opencode sessions and, as an example, compact any session idle after 3 hours that has never been compacted.

I fixed the issue with PR #29815.

When the model emits text-start followed immediately by a tool call (without any text-delta in between), the text-end handler was writing an empty text part to the database. The fix adds a guard at text-end: only persist the text part if its content has length > 0. Since updatePart is a full-row overwrite, skipping it when text is empty leaves the row in its previous state.
